newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tofas plant to operate single shift.
newsitem.headline: Tofas plant to operate single shift.

text.p: Turkey's leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi said it planned to introduce a single work shift at its Bursa plant instead of the current two shifts.

In a statement sent to the Istanbul Stock Exchange, Tofas said falling car demand due to expectations of cheaper imports following a recent government decree to ease import rules "brought up the subject of a single-shift operation instead of two to the stage of practice".
Tofas said a one shift reduction would involve around 1,000 workers, or 22 percent of the factory's total workforce and would lead to a 30 percent drop in the plant's production capacity.
It added that talks were underway with the workers' union Turk Metal to find "the most suitable solution" on how to go ahead with the shift reduction.
Car and part producers as well as labour unions in Turkey's automotive sector have been strongly opposing a cabinet decree which went into effect on October 24 to ease car import rules.

The decree allows some three million expatriate Turkish workers in Europe to import cars and machinery of up to four years of age without customs duties, if they deposit a minimum of 50,000 marks for one year at state-owned Ziraat Bank.

Expatriates who open the minimum account by end-1996 will be allowed to bring in one duty free foreign car or 50,000 marks worth machinery from June 1, 1997. They will also receive a 10 percent annual interest on their deposits.
The Anatolian agency reported on Wednesday that such accounts totalling 42 million marks have so far been opened at Ziraat Bank.
The government forecasts 25,000 duty free car imports and an income of 1.3 billion marks from the scheme as part of its two revenue raising packages revealed since late July.
Turkey's car output plunged 32 percent from a year ago to 17,350 units in October and fell by seven percent to 172,964 in January-October, when compared to the same 1995 period.
